run.script_question: Cross-region uniqueness with the prefix actually load-bearing - do three independent per-region deployments issue colliding raw numbers that only the prefix separates?
run.executed_by: Cortex Code (sql_execute, one statement per call)
run.halt_gate: T6.1 returned 'STOP - no collision. Deployments are not independent; T6.2 would be VACUOUS.' The script instructs: '>>> IF THIS SAYS STOP, DO NOT RUN T6.2. Report it and investigate. <<<' That instruction was followed.
run.teardown_skip_reason: Teardown intentionally not run, consistent with all previous runs. NOTE: this run created three NEW SCHEMAS in LM_POC_DB (W6_RGN_NA, W6_RGN_EU, W6_RGN_APAC) which are outside the usual POC_SCHEMA scratch area. Cleanup SQL is listed.
run.headline: R12 IS STILL NOT PROVEN, but the cause is now a far more important one than in 05. The script's central premise - that an UNQUALIFIED sequence reference inside a SQL UDF resolves 'in the schema containing the function' - IS FALSE. Sequence references resolve against the CALLER'S CURRENT SCHEMA at run time, while TABLE references in the same function body resolve against the FUNCTION'S schema. The resolution is asymmetric. See finding F19.
notes_on_completeness: query_id and elapsed_ms are null for every statement: no QUERY_HISTORY lookup was performed. No values were inferred or fabricated.
Five diagnostic statements not present in the script were added (seq 24, 26, 28, 30, 31) to establish the root cause of the T6.1 STOP. Each is marked as added.
T6.2, T6.2a, T6.2b and T6.3 were NOT RUN, because the script forbids running them after a T6.1 STOP.

T6.4 and T6.5 were NOT RUN. T6.4 reads w6_global_keys, which T6.2 would have populated and which is empty. T6.5's own header asserts it is 'NOW meaningful, because the raw values genuinely overlap' - that premise is false, so running it would have produced a figure presented on a false basis.
The parallel-session runner was NOT invoked for this run. No concurrency claim is made anywhere in this file.

statements.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION w6_regional_key(region_name VARCHAR)
RETURNS NUMBER(38,0) VOLATILE
COMMENT = 'Identical text in every region schema. Unqualified names resolve locally (R8).'
AS $$
    CAST((SELECT m.REGION_CODE FROM w6_region_map m WHERE m.REGION_NAME = region_name)
         * 1000000000000000 + w6_employee_seq.NEXTVAL AS NUMBER(38,0))
$$
statements.observation: The COMMENT asserts the premise under test. The diagnostics at seq 24-31 show that assertion is only half correct.

statements.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION w6_raw_key()
RETURNS NUMBER(38,0) VOLATILE
AS $$ w6_employee_seq.NEXTVAL $$
statements.observation: This function names ONLY a sequence and no table, which makes it the clean instrument for isolating sequence resolution.

RETURNS NUMBER(38,0) VOLATILE

USE SCHEMA POC_SCHEMA
statements.observation: CRITICAL IN HINDSIGHT. The script switches the caller's schema to POC_SCHEMA here and then calls the three regions' functions by qualified name. Because sequence references resolve against the CALLER'S schema (finding F19), every subsequent probe drew from POC_SCHEMA's sequence rather than from the three regional ones.

statements.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_out,
       COUNT(DISTINCT RAW_K) AS distinct_raw,
       COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT RAW_K) AS collisions,
       CASE WHEN COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT RAW_K) > 0
            THEN 'SENSITIVITY OK - regions collide without a prefix, so the prefix can be tested'
            ELSE 'STOP - no collision. Deployments are not independent; T6.2 would be VACUOUS.'
       END AS verdict
FROM w6_raw_probe

findings.title: In a SQL UDF body, SEQUENCE references resolve against the CALLER'S current schema while TABLE references resolve against the FUNCTION'S schema
findings.evidence: Four independent observations. (1) Seq 30: after 1500 rows drawn through the three regional functions, all three regional sequences remained at NEXT_VALUE 1 while POC_SCHEMA's sequence advanced to 1901 - POC_SCHEMA being the caller's schema throughout T6.1. (2) Seq 31: calling W6_RGN_NA's function from EU's schema returned region code 1, so the table came from NA's schema. (3) Seq 32: the same function asked for 'APAC' returned NULL even though APAC's own map contains APAC, proving the table read was NA's map and not the caller's; and seq 33 shows EU's and APAC's sequences each advanced to 101 while NA's stayed at 1. (4) Seq 34: calling NA's function from GOLD_POC, which has no sequence of that name, fails with "invalid identifier 'W6_EMPLOYEE_SEQ.NEXTVAL'" despite W6_RGN_NA.W6_EMPLOYEE_SEQ existing.
findings.interpretation: The two unqualified identifiers in one function body are resolved by different rules. The table follows the documented 'resolved in the schema containing the function' behaviour. The sequence does not - it is resolved in the caller's current schema at run time, and raises invalid identifier if absent there.
findings.implication: This refutes the premise stated in the script's header at lines 22-25 and in every function's COMMENT. It also means R2's T2.1b did NOT establish what it was taken to establish: in that test the function, the sequence and the caller were all in POC_SCHEMA, so it could not distinguish the two rules. The practical consequence is severe - a region's function does not carry its sequence with it. Which sequence is consumed depends on session state, so the same function invoked from two differently-configured sessions silently draws from two different sequences, or fails outright.
findings.status: Open - CRITICAL. This needs to go to the design team before any per-region deployment approach is settled. Recommend also correcting R2's F-series note that treats T2.1b as proof of portability.

findings.title: The T6.1 probe only ran at all because a leftover object from the R2 run happened to have the right name
findings.evidence: Seq 28: North America's probe started at 101, which is exactly where the R2 run left POC_SCHEMA.W6_EMPLOYEE_SEQ (recorded in the R2 evidence file as NEXT_VALUE 101). Seq 34 shows that without a same-named sequence in the caller's schema the call raises invalid identifier.
findings.interpretation: Had teardown been run after R2, POC_SCHEMA would have held no W6_EMPLOYEE_SEQ and T6.1 would have failed with a compilation error rather than returning plausible-looking numbers. The run produced 1500 clean rows and a confident STOP verdict only by coincidence of naming.
findings.implication: A direct cost of the standing decision to skip teardown. More importantly it is a near-miss: an error would have been investigated immediately, whereas plausible numbers invited the assumption that the deployments were working. Recommend either running teardown between packs, or using run-scoped object names so cross-pack name collisions cannot occur.

findings.title: To make R12 testable, each concurrent session must set its own current schema to its region's schema
findings.evidence: Derived from F19. Seq 33 shows that when the caller's schema is W6_RGN_EU the EU sequence advances, and when it is W6_RGN_APAC the APAC sequence advances - each from 1.
findings.interpretation: Caller-schema resolution is not merely an obstacle; it is also the mechanism that makes the test work, provided the harness uses it deliberately. If session A runs USE SCHEMA W6_RGN_NA, session B USE SCHEMA W6_RGN_EU and session C USE SCHEMA W6_RGN_APAC, then each draws from its own sequence starting at 1, the raw values genuinely collide, and T6.1's gate would open.
findings.implication: This is a small harness change, not a design change: the per-session USE SCHEMA already exists in runner/run_parallel.ps1 and only needs to vary per worksheet. It would also mirror production more faithfully, since each region's ETL would connect with its own default schema. Note however that it makes the correctness of the key dependent on session configuration, which is a genuine fragility worth stating in the build standard regardless of whether the test then passes.
findings.status: Open - ready to execute on request. This would close the R12 gate.

findings.title: The sensitivity-gate design worked and should be retained
findings.evidence: 04's T4.7 and 05's T5.2 both returned uniqueness PASS while being insensitive to the property under test. 06's T6.1 gate detected the broken premise and halted before any uniqueness claim was made.
findings.interpretation: Three runs, three broken premises, but only the third caught itself. The difference is that 06 asserts a precondition rather than only a postcondition.
findings.implication: Keep the gate pattern. Recommend retrofitting an equivalent precondition check into 04 and 05 so their recorded passes cannot be quoted without the caveat, and adopting 06's T6.3 raw-value-reuse check as a standing requirement for any future cross-region uniqueness claim.
